basis: Oxidative phosphorylation disorder presenting as mitochondrial myopathy; progressive weakness and abnormal muscle histology in 1/1 reported patient.
Glycosylation defect with defining neurodevelopmental and hepatic dysfunction; coagulation abnormalities 80-99%. Common ocular and bone findings omitted at cap.
Intestinal methionine transport disorder; intellectual disability and seizures are characteristic neurologic manifestations, although frequencies are unspecified.
Central neurodevelopmental disorder with spasticity, dystonia and impaired myelination; weakness and abnormal tone do not establish primary muscle disease.
Developmental delay and intellectual disability define the syndrome; cardiac, ocular and hearing abnormalities are below 30%. Cryptorchidism has no applicable axis.
Parasitic infestation occupying or burrowing into the epidermis; skin location and infectious mechanism define the group.
Neurodevelopmental syndrome; structural cardiac septal abnormalities occur in 30-79%. Renal and hearing abnormalities are reported in only 5-29%.
Intellectual disability, congenital heart defects and skeletal/muscle malformations define the syndrome; strabismus 80-99% and ptosis 30-79%. Dental abnormalities omitted at cap.
Neutrophil oxidative-burst defect; intrinsic granulomatous intestinal inflammation affects roughly 30-50% in CGD. Separately diagnosed infections do not add organ axes.
Familial immune hyperinflammation with hemophagocytosis and cytopenias; hepatitis and intellectual disability each reported in 1/1 patient; subtype evidence is limited.
Isolated developmental eye disorder; microphthalmia and corneal stromal opacity in 6/6 patients.
Hypertrichosis affects the eyelid; both the named ocular adnexal location and the hair disorder define this concept.
CA2 deficiency defines osteopetrosis and renal tubular acidosis; neurologic dysfunction with cerebral calcification is a defining feature, with developmental delay in 30-79%.
Chronic immune-mediated choroidal inflammation and posterior uveitis; choroidal vascular involvement remains within the ocular axis.
Nephrosis and urinary tract anomalies, deafness, and thumb/hallux skeletal malformations define the syndrome; corresponding anomalies are reported in 30-79%.
Immune-mediated skeletal muscle rippling combined with myasthenia gravis, an autoimmune neuromuscular junction disorder.
Germ cell tumour arising in the testis; reproductive tumour origin does not establish endocrine gland dysfunction.
Intellectual disability and speech delay in 7/7 define the syndrome. Constipation and eyelid edema in 3/7 do not demonstrate direct organ damage.
Skin/nail keratinization disorder; chronic blepharitis or keratoconjunctivitis sicca and anal mucosal leukoplakia are each reported as frequent (30-79%).
Lethal skeletal dysplasia; the severely shortened thorax causes respiratory failure/asphyxia in the characteristic neonatal course.
Autosomal dominant intellectual disability defines the disease; frequencies of associated exotropia and digital anomalies are insufficient to support additional axes.
Mitochondrial encephalomyopathy defines metabolic, brain and skeletal muscle dysfunction; marrow hypocellularity is occasional (5-29%), so haematologic involvement is omitted.
Protein O-glycosylation metabolic disorder; skeletal myopathy characterizes most represented subtypes. Brain and ocular involvement vary across the umbrella.
Malignant fibroblastic tumour of soft connective tissue and bone; organ-specific visceral subtypes do not establish involvement across the umbrella.
Vestibular system dysfunction defines the ataxia; vestibular function belongs to the otologic axis, with no established additional CNS lesion.
